_: What this repository can prove about itself, measured by ratchet.py against the
repository rather than read off a document.
It exists because this package is a submodule of a production application and,
until this file, nothing ran its suite except a person on a laptop. A harness
that governs other projects and is not governed itself teaches every project
that consumes it that the floor is optional.
Baseline measured 2026-08-24, Python 3.11 on Windows, installed as
`pip install -e .[test]` — pydantic and pytest, NO anthropic and NO openai.
That environment is the point and not an accident: it is what CI installs, and
every number below is only meaningful next to it.
_kinds: floor    may rise, may never fall
exact    must equal, and a change in EITHER direction has to be deliberate
ceiling  may fall, may never rise past the tolerance in ratchet.py
recorded measured every run, gates nothing

`anthropic` and `openai` are OPTIONAL extras. A module-level import of either
turns an extra into a requirement for everybody who installs the base package,
and it does so silently — the failure appears at import time in whatever process

Measured by walking the AST of every file under src/, deferred imports included,
because all four of them are written inside functions and a check reading only
the top of each file would report zero and be wrong in the reassuring direction.
Exact rather than a ceiling: a deferred import REMOVED is also a change worth
explaining, and only an exact count makes both directions show up in a diff.
_tests_skipped: Eight, and they are named because an unnamed skip is how a guard stops running
without anybody deciding that it should.
6  tests/test_bubblewrap_sandbox.py   bubblewrap is a Linux-only jail
2  tests/test_anthropic_sdk_pin.py    the anthropic extra is not installed
The second one is a hole rather than a fact of life: it is the best guard in the
repo -- it introspects messages.create on the INSTALLED sdk instead of parsing a
version string -- and it skips in exactly the environment where a wrong pin is
picked up blind. CI therefore runs a second job WITH the extra and sets
HARNESS_REQUIRE_PROVIDER_EXTRAS=1, which turns that skip into a failure. And a
second guard, tests/test_declared_pin.py, checks the DECLARED string in
pyproject.toml and imports nothing but the standard library, so it can never be
RAISED 7 -> 8 on 2026-08-24, and this is what the exact count is for. The guard
moved from a module-level `pytest.importorskip` -- one skip for the whole file --
to a `pytestmark.skipif`, which reports one per test function. Same coverage, and
the number now counts assertions that did not run rather than files that did not
load, which is the quantity worth watching.
